<result>pr:
## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #&lt;N&gt;`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

   ```markdown
   ## Test Evidence

   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
   ```

   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
   - **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
   - AI may draft this section; the author checks that it is accurate.

5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** &lt;shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why&gt;

   **Encountered:** &lt;tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it&gt;
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** &lt;what you ran or tried&gt;

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Mutation testing (D6)

A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.

**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.

| Code changed | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
   project.
2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.

Files:

- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;github-username&gt;.md`, using the template below.
- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;github-username&gt;-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=&lt;file&gt;.json`.
  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.

Common problems:

- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated
  files. Otherwise mutants they would catch show as survived or not covered. Check that the
  relevant tests ran before writing a new tes

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

Refs #155

## What changed

This is the D6 mutation testing deliverable for #155, whose PR #162 is already merged, so this PR doesn't close the issue. It changes no product code.

- `web_src/js/features/repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts`: two new tests, `suggestionInsertPos fence edge cases` and `initSuggestChangeButton in a form`, which kill 9 of the 15 mutants that survived StrykerJS
- `docs/sprint3/mutation/155-controlled-opposition.md`: the write-up, with every survivor analysed and the three questions answered
- `docs/sprint3/mutation/controlled-opposition.stryker.config.mjs`: my Stryker config, following ab-wm's pattern
- `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/155-controlled-opposition-{before,after}.json`: the two reports

The mutation score went from 81.10% to 88.19% (87.29% to 94.92% on covered code). The 6 survivors left are 3 equivalent mutants, 1 that is equivalent in practice and 2 narrow cases that aren't worth a test; the write-up explains each one.

## Why

The D6 deliverable asks for a mutation tool run on one issue's PR, an analysis of its survivors, and at least one test that kills a survivor revealing a gap. The survivors showed the #162 tests checked the cases the ACs list but not CommonMark's fence rules, and that the click tests never put the button in a form or the cursor in the middle of the text.

## Test Evidence

The PR adds tests only, so each row is a case the old tests missed.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC2: the block starts on a line of its own, and the text after it is kept | `initSuggestChangeButton in a form` (cursor in the middle of `ab\n`) | unit | AC |
| AC12: a second block never goes inside an existing one | `suggestionInsertPos fence edge cases` (short tilde runs, a run after other text, a tilde fence with a backtick in its info string, a shorter closing fence, a closing fence followed by spaces, an unclosed fence on the last line) | unit | AC, docs (CommonMark 0.31.2, section 4.5) |
| No AC: clicking the button doesn't submit the comment form | `initSuggestChangeButton in a form` (the click event is cancelled) | unit | docs (HTML spec: a `&lt;button&gt;` with no `type` submits its form) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** None.

**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote both new tests. I checked their expected values against AC2, AC12, CommonMark section 4.5 and the HTML spec. Both passed on the unchanged source before the second Stryker run, and every mutant the write-up says they kill shows as killed in the after report.

## CI / manual verification

Locally: `pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts` passes 8/8, ESLint is clean on the test file, and both Stryker runs finished without errors (about 10 seconds each). The command is in the write-up.

## Design

No design change. Mutating only the two lines PR #162 changed in `repo-issue.ts` (`--mutate` line ranges) keeps the run on the PR's own code instead of the whole 300-line file.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** None.

**Encountered:** The fence regex on line 30 of `repo-diff-suggestion.ts` ends in `(.*)$`, and `.` doesn't match U+2028 or U+2029, so a fence line holding either one isn't recognised. CommonMark doesn't treat those characters as line endings, so it would. A Stryker survivor exposed this; I left the source alone because this PR changes tests only, and the write-up records it.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) wrote the Stryker config from ab-wm's pattern, ran both Stryker runs, sorted the survivors into test gaps and equivalent mutants, wrote both tests and drafted the write-up. I reviewed the survivor verdicts and the tests' expected values against the ACs and specs before approving each commit. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on #155.

Closes #181

## What changed

This changes CI configuration only, with no product code.

- The four `release-*` workflows have `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` on every job, so on this fork they show as skipped.
- `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` also run on pushes to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and from Run workflow with a `ref` input, which every checkout uses. On those events every suite runs; pull requests still filter by `files-changed`.
- Concurrency: pull requests keep their per-branch group. Pushes to `main` share the group `<workflow>-refs/heads/main` with `cancel-in-progress` off, so a running suite is never cancelled and only the waiting run gets replaced. Tag and manual runs each get a group of their own.
- `files-changed.yml` skips detection on anything but a pull request, so the job always succeeds and every output is empty there.
- `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. The gobuild key is now `gobuild-<os>-<arch>-<go.sum hash>-<sha>`, PR jobs fall back to the newest entry, and the seeder has no fallback, so it builds clean. It warms `-race -cover` for the normal tags.
- The `gogit` unit pass moved to a new job, `test-unit-gogit`. Both unit jobs run `make test-check`; only `test-unit` uploads Go coverage.
- Vitest coverage moved to `test-frontend-coverage`, which has no `needs`. `sonarqube` needs it and `test-unit`, downloads both reports, and runs only for same-repo pull requests and pushes to `main`.
- Every job with steps in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml` has a job-level `timeout-minutes` from 20 to 60. The two `cache-seeder` jobs got one too.
- Updated `sonar-project.properties`, `.claude-students/docs/build-and-tooling.md` and its guide twin.

## Why

`main` was red on every push because of release workflows that can't run here, it never ran the integration or e2e suites, and backend PRs took about 27.6 minutes, mostly compiling against a cache 141 commits old and running the two unit passes back to back. This covers AC1 to AC8 of #181. AC7's timing can only be measured once this is on `main` and the cache has been saved.

Follows the four Design Decisions in #181, with three changes:

Closes #181

## What changed

This changes CI configuration only, with no product code.

- The four `release-*` workflows have `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` on every job, so on this fork they show as skipped.
- `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` also run on pushes to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and from Run workflow with a `ref` input, which every checkout uses. On those events every suite runs; pull requests still filter by `files-changed`.
- Concurrency: pull requests keep their per-branch group. Pushes to `main` share the group `<workflow>-refs/heads/main` with `cancel-in-progress` off, so a running suite is never cancelled and only the waiting run gets replaced. Tag and manual runs each get a group of their own.
- `files-changed.yml` skips detection on anything but a pull request, so the job always succeeds and every output is empty there.

- **Known flake:** this is #171, which is open and unassigned. It fails when `shortcut.test.ts` and `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` happen to share a Vitest worker. #181 lists it as out of scope and names this same test as the one that turned `main` red unnoticed.
- **Same code, different result:** the compliance `frontend` job in this same push ran the full Vitest suite on the same commit and passed.
- **Not caused by this PR:** the PR changes no TypeScript. The only difference is that Vitest now runs in its own job instead of inside `sonarqube`, which is AC6 working as intended. Before, this failure would have shown up only as a failed `sonarqube` job.
- **Coverage:** with the test failing, Vitest wrote no `lcov.info`, so the upload only warned. `sonarqube` will scan without TypeScript coverage this time, as designed.

The other checks had passed or were still running when I looked; none had failed.

Should I re-run the failed job with `gh run rerun 43677647631 --failed`? That leaves #171 unfixed, so this test can fail again on later runs until someone takes that issue.

bot:
---
name: coderabbit-behaviour
description: "Review bots on this fork: CodeRabbit (one auto review per PR, bare `@coderabbitai review` to re-run, auto-resolves addressed threads), plus Gitar and SonarQube Cloud since 2026-11-05."
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Config is `.coderabbit.yaml` at the repo root; course-specific checks live under `reviews.pre_merge_checks.custom_checks` and `reviews.path_instructions`. Seen on PR #94, 2026-10-15:

- `auto_incremental_review: false`, so it reviews once when the PR opens. A push does not trigger another review. Post `@coderabbitai review` to get one.
- Keep that command comment bare, with no attribution line, so the bot doesn't read extra text as a chat message.
- After a fix commit it edits each thread to "✅ Addressed in commit &lt;sha&gt;" and resolves the thread itself. Check `isResolved` with GraphQL before resolving by hand.
- Its pre-merge results ("Passed checks: N passed") are in the summary issue comment, not in the review body.
- It quotes the course site in its findings, so verify each one against the page; on #94 all three were real gaps.
- The plan allows about 10 reviews per hour.

- **Gitar** (`gitar-bot`, PR #148): instructions in `.gitar/review/course.md`, checks in `.gitar/rules/` (commit messages, skipped tests need an issue, test expected values). First seen reviewing PR #147.

```markdown
Closes #181

## What changed

This changes CI configuration only, with no product code.

- The four `release-*` workflows have `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` on every job, so on this fork they show as skipped.
- `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` also run on pushes to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and from Run workflow with a `ref` input, which every checkout uses. On those events every suite runs; pull requests still filter by `files-changed`.
- Concurrency: pull requests keep their per-branch group. Pushes to `main` share the group `<workflow>-refs/heads/main` with `cancel-in-progress` off, so a running suite is never cancelled and only the waiting run gets replaced. Tag and manual runs each get a group of their own.
- `files-changed.yml` skips detection on anything but a pull request, so the job always succeeds and every output is empty there.
- `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. The gobuild key is now `gobuild-<os>-<arch>-<go.sum hash>-<sha>`, PR jobs fall back to the newest entry, and the seeder has no fallback, so it builds clean. It warms `-race -cover` for the normal tags.
- The `gogit` unit pass moved to a new job, `test-unit-gogit`. Both unit jobs run `make test-check`; only `test-unit` uploads Go coverage.
- Vitest coverage moved to `test-frontend-coverage`, which has no `needs`. `sonarqube` needs it and `test-unit`, downloads both reports, and runs only for same-repo pull requests and pushes to `main`.
- Every job with steps in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml` has a job-level `timeout-minutes` from 20 to 60. The two `cache-seeder` jobs got one too.
- Updated `sonar-project.properties`, `.claude-students/docs/build-and-tooling.md` and its guide twin.

## Why

`main` was red on every push because of release workflows that can't run here, it never ran the integration or e2e suites, and backend PRs took about 27.6 minutes, mostly compiling against a cache 141 commits old and running the two unit passes back to back. This covers AC1 to AC8 of #181. AC7's timing can only be measured once this is on `main` and the cache has been saved.

## Test Evidence

This PR changes no product behaviour, so there are no automated tests. Each AC is checked from CI runs after merge, as the issue's Evidence of Fix section plans, and the results go in a comment on #181.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: release workflows skipped on `main` and `v1.*` tags | Manual, after merge: the first push to `main` shows `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` as skipped. `release-tag-rc` and `release-tag-version` are checked in the diff, and `release-tag-version` again at the s3 tag | manual | AC |
| AC2: every suite runs on each merge, and a waiting run is replaced, never a running one | Manual, after merge: the push run on `main` runs every `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` job; two merges in a row show the replaced waiting run as cancelled | manual | AC |
| AC3: Run workflow and sprint tags run every suite in their own group | Manual, after merge: Run workflow on `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` with `ref` `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` | manual | AC |
| AC4: cache saved per commit with `-race -cover`; first package result within 1 min | Manual, after merge: the seeder run saves `gobuild-…-<sha>`; a backend PR's `test-unit` log shows the first `ok` line no more than 1 min after `make test-backend` starts | manual | AC |
| AC5: normal and `gogit` passes in parallel jobs | Manual, after merge: `test-unit` and `test-unit-gogit` run side by side on the first backend PR (this PR changes no Go files, so both are skipped here); both end with `make test-check` | manual | AC |
| AC6: Vitest in its own job, `sonarqube` scans both reports, skipped on tags and manual runs | Manual: on this PR, `test-frontend-coverage` starts as soon as the run does and `sonarqube` reports TypeScript coverage; after merge, a backend PR shows it running alongside the unit jobs with both coverages scanned, and the manual run from AC3 shows `sonarqube` skipped | manual | AC |
| AC7: median `db-tests` time of four backend PR runs at most 22 min | Manual, after merge: time four first-attempt backend PR runs where no job waited over 1 min | manual | AC, issue discussion (the target was set by measuring existing runs, 2026-11-13) |
| AC8: job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60 | Manual: the diff gives every job with steps in the three files a timeout of 20 to 60 | manual | AC |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** All ACs. They describe how GitHub Actions schedules and caches runs, which only a real run on GitHub can show, and most need this change on `main` first.

**AI-written tests:** None.

## CI / manual verification

Locally: `make lint-actions` (actionlint) reports no findings, `yamllint` on the changed YAML files is clean, and `./.claude-students/check.sh` passes. This PR touches no Go files, so its `db-tests` run only runs `test-sqlite` (it filters on `actions`), `test-frontend-coverage` and `sonarqube`; the unit and database jobs are skipped as before.

## Design

Follows the four Design Decisions in #181, with three changes:

- **Seeder build flags.** The seeder warms `-race -cover` for the normal tags in place of plain `-race`, because no job runs the normal tags without coverage any more. The `gogit` build still warms plain `-race`. Rejected: keeping plain `-race` only, which leaves `test-unit` compiling the coverage build from scratch and misses AC4; and warming both `-race` and `-race -cover` as the issue's wording allows, which makes each cache entry bigger for a build nothing restores.
- **Concurrency group for `main`.** The group is `<workflow>-refs/heads/main`. A fork PR from its own `main` branch has `head_ref` `main`, and with `cancel-in-progress` on, it would cancel our `main` run. Rejected: `<workflow>-main`, which has that collision; and prefixing the pull request group (`<workflow>-pr-<head_ref>`), which also avoids it but changes the PR group the issue says to keep.
- **`sonarqube` keeps installing frontend dependencies.** Only the Vitest run moved out, so the TypeScript analysis can read types from `node_modules` as it did before. Rejected: skipping the install, which saves about a minute but can change what the scan reports and isn't on the critical path; and passing `node_modules` from `test-frontend-coverage` as an artifact, which adds a large upload and download for no time saved.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** `test-unit-gogit` copies `test-unit`'s service containers, about 40 lines, so a change to one has to go into the other. A matrix would share them, but the two passes need different `GOEXPERIMENT` handling and only one uploads coverage. The `cache-seeder` `lint` job now runs on every merge too, though its golangci-lint cache key only changes with `go.sum` or `.golangci.yml`.

**Encountered:** The golangci-lint cache has the same key problem the gobuild cache had: it can't be overwritten until `go.sum` or `.golangci.yml` changes. Speeding up `lint-backend` is out of scope for #181, so I left it.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) wrote the workflow and action changes from the issue's ACs and Design Decisions, ran actionlint, yamllint and check.sh, and drafted this description. I reviewed the diff against each AC before approving the commit. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on #181.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

```markdown
Closes #181

## What changed

This changes CI configuration only, with no product code.

- The four `release-*` workflows have `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` on every job, so on this fork they show as skipped.
- `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` also run on pushes to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and from Run workflow with a `ref` input, which every checkout uses. On those events every suite runs; pull requests still filter by `files-changed`.
- Concurrency: pull requests keep their per-branch group. Pushes to `main` share the group `<workflow>-refs/heads/main` with `cancel-in-progress` off, so a running suite is never cancelled and only the waiting run gets replaced. Tag and manual runs each get a group of their own.
- `files-changed.yml` skips detection on anything but a pull request, so the job always succeeds and every output is empty there.
- `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. The gobuild key is now `gobuild-<os>-<arch>-<go.sum hash>-<sha>`, PR jobs fall back to the newest entry, and the seeder has no fallback, so it builds clean. It warms `-race -cover` for the normal tags.
- The `gogit` unit pass moved to a new job, `test-unit-gogit`. Both unit jobs run `make test-check`; only `test-unit` uploads Go coverage.
- Vitest coverage moved to `test-frontend-coverage`, which has no `needs`. `sonarqube` needs it and `test-unit`, downloads both reports, and runs only for same-repo pull requests and pushes to `main`.
- Every job with steps in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml` has a job-level `timeout-minutes` from 20 to 60. The two `cache-seeder` jobs got one too.
- Updated `sonar-project.properties`, `.claude-students/docs/build-and-tooling.md` and its guide twin.

## Why

`main` was red on every push because of release workflows that can't run here, it never ran the integration or e2e suites, and backend PRs took about 27.6 minutes, mostly compiling against a cache 141 commits old and running the two unit passes back to back. This covers AC1 to AC8 of #181. AC7's timing can only be measured once this is on `main` and the cache has been saved.

## Test Evidence

This PR changes no product behaviour, so there are no automated tests. Each AC is checked from CI runs after merge, as the issue's Evidence of Fix section plans, and the results go in a comment on #181.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: release workflows skipped on `main` and `v1.*` tags | Manual, after merge: the first push to `main` shows `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` as skipped. `release-tag-rc` and `release-tag-version` are checked in the diff, and `release-tag-version` again at the s3 tag | manual | AC |
| AC2: every suite runs on each merge, and a waiting run is replaced, never a running one | Manual, after merge: the push run on `main` runs every `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` job; two merges in a row show the replaced waiting run as cancelled | manual | AC |
| AC3: Run workflow and sprint tags run every suite in their own group | Manual, after merge: Run workflow on `db-tests` and `e2e-tests` with `ref` `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` | manual | AC |
| AC4: cache saved per commit with `-race -cover`; first package result within 1 min | Manual, after merge: the seeder run saves `gobuild-…-<sha>`; a backend PR's `test-unit` log shows the first `ok` line no more than 1 min after `make test-backend` starts | manual | AC |
| AC5: normal and `gogit` passes in parallel jobs | Manual, after merge: `test-unit` and `test-unit-gogit` run side by side on the first backend PR (this PR changes no Go files, so both are skipped here); both end with `make test-check` | manual | AC |
| AC6: Vitest in its own job, `sonarqube` scans both reports, skipped on tags and manual runs | Manual: on this PR, `test-frontend-coverage` starts as soon as the run does and `sonarqube` reports TypeScript coverage; after merge, a backend PR shows it running alongside the unit jobs with both coverages scanned, and the manual run from AC3 shows `sonarqube` skipped | manual | AC |
| AC7: median `db-tests` time of four backend PR runs at most 22 min | Manual, after merge: time four first-attempt backend PR runs where no job waited over 1 min | manual | AC, issue discussion (the target was set by measuring existing runs, 2026-11-13) |
| AC8: job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60 | Manual: the diff gives every job with steps in the three files a timeout of 20 to 60 | manual | AC |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** All ACs. They describe how GitHub Actions schedules and caches runs, which only a real run on GitHub can show, and most need this change on `main` first.

**AI-written tests:** None.

## CI / manual verification

Locally: `make lint-actions` (actionlint) reports no findings, `yamllint` on the changed YAML files is clean, and `./.claude-students/check.sh` passes. This PR touches no Go files, so its `db-tests` run only runs `test-sqlite` (it filters on `actions`), `test-frontend-coverage` and `sonarqube`; the unit and database jobs are skipped as before.

## Design

Follows the four Design Decisions in #181, with four changes:

- **Seeder build flags.** The seeder warms `-race -cover` for the normal tags in place of plain `-race`, because no job runs the normal tags without coverage any more. The `gogit` build still warms plain `-race`. Rejected: keeping plain `-race` only, which leaves `test-unit` compiling the coverage build from scratch and misses AC4; and warming both `-race` and `-race -cover` as the issue's wording allows, which makes each cache entry bigger for a build nothing restores.
- **Concurrency group for `main`.** The group is `<workflow>-refs/heads/main`. A fork PR from its own `main` branch has `head_ref` `main`, and with `cancel-in-progress` on, it would cancel our `main` run. Rejected: `<workflow>-main`, which has that collision; and prefixing the pull request group (`<workflow>-pr-<head_ref>`), which also avoids it but changes the PR group the issue says to keep.
- **`sonarqube` keeps installing frontend dependencies.** Only the Vitest run moved out, so the TypeScript analysis can read types from `node_modules` as it did before. Rejected: skipping the install, which saves about a minute but can change what the scan reports and isn't on the critical path; and passing `node_modules` from `test-frontend-coverage` as an artifact, which adds a large upload and download for no time saved.
- **Seeder runs are no longer cancelled.** Decision 3 let a newer seeder run cancel the older one, but a cancelled run saves nothing and a clean build takes about 30 minutes, so merges landing closer together than that would never refresh the cache. `cancel-in-progress` is now false: a running seeder finishes and saves, and a newer push only replaces the waiting run. Rejected: keeping the cancel, which can starve the cache during a burst of merges; and a per-commit group, which runs every queued seeder and adds a 30-minute job per merge against the org's 20-job limit.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** `test-unit-gogit` copies `test-unit`'s service containers, about 40 lines, so a change to one has to go into the other. A matrix would share them, but the two passes need different `GOEXPERIMENT` handling and only one uploads coverage. The `cache-seeder` `lint` job now runs on every merge too, though its golangci-lint cache key only changes with `go.sum` or `.golangci.yml`.

**Encountered:** The golangci-lint cache has the same key problem the gobuild cache had: it can't be overwritten until `go.sum` or `.golangci.yml` changes. Speeding up `lint-backend` is out of scope for #181, so I left it.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) wrote the workflow and action changes from the issue's ACs and Design Decisions, ran actionlint, yamllint and check.sh, and drafted this description. I reviewed the diff against each AC before approving the commit. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on #181.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---
name: ai-log-tooling
description: "How AI logs get filed here (`.claude/bin/ai-log`, SessionEnd sync hook, `/file-ai-logs`), the sprint date table, and SpecStory quirks."
metadata:

  modified: 2026-11-04T22:43:35.027Z
---

Built 2026-10-06. It's all local-only, because `.claude/` is gitignored. The rules themselves are in `ai-logs/README.md`.

- **`.claude/bin/ai-log &lt;slug&gt; [session-id] [--sprint N] [--dry-run]`, and `--list`:**
  - Runs `specstory sync claude -s &lt;id&gt; --no-cloud-sync`.
  - Finds the transcript by its `&lt;!-- Claude Code Session &lt;id&gt; (...Z) --&gt;` header, looking only in the first 5 lines because transcripts quote other sessions' ids.
  - Copies it byte for byte to `ai-logs/sprint&lt;N&gt;/controlled-opposition/&lt;LOCAL start date&gt;_claude-code_&lt;slug&gt;.md`.
  - A dry run reproduced all four hand-filed logs exactly.
- **Sprint table:** the `SPRINTS` dates come from the course schedule, fetched 2026-10-06: S0 09-01..09-17, S1 09-22..10-08, S2 10-13..10-29, S3 11-03..11-19, S4 11-24..12-15. S4 ends Dec 15 per /schedule/; /sprints/ says Dec 10. A date between sprints errors out and needs `--sprint`.
- **Sync hook:** `.claude/settings.local.json` has a SessionEnd hook that runs `.claude/bin/specstory-sync-hook`, which syncs the ending session into `.specstory/history/`.
- **`/file-ai-logs` skill:**
  - lists unfiled sessions, skips the current one and command-only ones, and proposes slugs
  - files them after the user's OK and commits only with approval
  - drafts the issue comment

SpecStory quirks:
- Pass `--no-cloud-sync`; `sync` otherwise uploads to SpecStory Cloud when logged in.
- Don't use `--print`, which writes an "Update Available" banner to stdout.
- SpecStory's own filename can take its slug from a subagent prompt (#61 exported as `…-you-are-reviewing-uncommitted.md`). Trust the session-id header, not the name.
- An export made mid-session stops at the export command. Rerun it after the session ends; it overwrites the same file.
- Some exported lines are CRLF. `.gitattributes` normalises them on commit, so ignore git's warning.
- The existing logs are verbatim exports. Never hand-write or summarise a log.

**Why:** Hand-copying logs was error-prone (UTC vs local dates, auto-generated slugs), and edited or incomplete logs are graded invalid.
What makes a log valid is in [[course-rules]].

**How to apply:** File logs with the script or skill, never by hand. Update `SPRINTS` when the schedule changes. See [[which-sessions-to-log]].

name: which-sessions-to-log
description: "File only sessions the course requires a log for (ones behind an issue's AI Assistance comment); never chase other unfiled sessions."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 71e5d7cd-352f-452d-834f-e857549a2dc3

Only care about sessions the class requires a log for: those that produced an issue deliverable that carries an AI Assistance comment. That means drafting an issue spec, implementing it, reviewing a PR or spec, and writing the sprint report. Everything else needs no log and no mention: general planning, "what are my issues" questions, requirement Q&amp;A, memory questions, AI tooling setup (pstack, verify skill, ai-log, SpecStory), and empty or `/clear` sessions. The user said so on 2026-10-06 (tooling) and on 2026-10-22: "not every single session in existence needs to be filed."

**Why:** Over-logging clutters the graded record, and listing every unfiled session as a to-do wastes the user's attention.
**How to apply:** When filing, consider only sessions tied to the issue or PR in question. Don't list other unfiled sessions as leftovers or remind the user about them. A short planning session that leads straight into one issue's work may go with that issue's logs, but only if the user wants it. When unsure, ask. See [[ai-log-tooling]].

Yes, file it now. A log covers a session, not the issue, so there's no reason to wait for the evidence. If you use AI for the evidence collection later, that's a separate session: file its log then and add it as row 2 in your AI Assistance comment by editing it.

Order:

1. **End this session first.** An export taken mid-session stops at the export command and leaves out the end of the conversation. Your SessionEnd hook syncs the full transcript when the session ends.
2. **File it from a new session** with `/file-ai-logs`. It copies the log to `ai-logs/sprint3/controlled-opposition/2026-11-15_claude-code_issue-181-impl.md` (or whatever slug you pick) and commits it with your approval.
3. **Put the log commit on `fix/issue-181-main-ci` before you request review.** That's how PR #180 did it (`chore(ai-log): …`). A push after a teammate approves resets their approval, so do it first. Otherwise you'll need a separate chore PR later.
4. **Post the AI Assistance comment on #181** with the log link pointing at the branch for now (`.../blob/fix/issue-181-main-ci/ai-logs/...`), since a `main` link would 404 until merge. Edit it to the `main` link after merge. Keep the log link out of the PR description, which already points at the issue comment.
